chunks: One of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Hakeem, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman who has despaired of menstruation: 'She is irrevocably divorced from him, and there is no waiting period for her'.
And it has been reported as well that: 'Upon her is the waiting period when she has been slept with'.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She is irrevocably divorced from him

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a menopausal woman who is divorced?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the iddah (waiting period) for menopausal women, establishing that while the default ruling is no iddah upon divorce, a waiting period is required if the marriage has been consummated. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the physiological cessation of menstruation as the marker for menopause, distinguishing it from pre-pubertal girls who have no iddah at all. The nuance highlights the juristic principle that consummation triggers the obligation of iddah even in the absence of menstrual cycles.
